title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 'équation des lacets' notes, Grothendieck studies the automorphism groups of the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}. These groups are close relatives of what is now called the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group. He relates them to the profinite modular group SL(2,Ẑ). The link is that the quotient of M_{0,4} = P^1−{0,1,∞} by S_3 is the j-line, with orbifold points of orders 2 and 3 and a cusp. The S_3 extension of π_{0,3} is then (up to ±1) the modular group; this is the group written Ĝ_{0,3}^+ → SL(2,Ẑ)'.

Previous page. Formula (45) gives a canonical homomorphism from M_{0,3}^{!~} to M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ. Here M_{0,3}^{!~} is the group of automorphisms respecting each of the three punctures, with the inertia/normalization conditions. M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) is a semi-direct product of 'torus' factors T_0, T_ρ(Ẑ), T_σ(Ẑ) (attached to the elliptic points of orders 2 and 3) with SL(2,Ẑ). Σ ≅ {±1}^3 is the product of the three sign subgroups. That map was built in two steps:
- the normalized subgroup M_{0,3}^{!~}(0) (normalizer of L_0, base point at 0) maps to SG*_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ_0;
- the decomposition (47), M^{!~} = M^{!~}(0)·π̂_{0,3}, together with π̂_{0,3} ↪ Ĝ_{0,3}^+ → SL(2,Ẑ)'.

This page. Grothendieck now passes to the full group M_{0,3}^~, which also allows the S_3 permutations of the three points.
- (48) gives a semi-direct product decomposition M_{0,3}^~ ≅ M_{0,3}^{!~}(ω) ⋊ Ĝ_{0,3}^+. Here the normalization is at ω, presumably an S_3-symmetric base point such as the order-3 orbifold point e^{iπ/3}. The finite or symmetric part is split off by the subgroup fixing that symmetric base point.
- Combining this directly with Ĝ_{0,3}^+ → SL(2,Ẑ)' gives (49), a homomorphism M_{0,3}^~ → (M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) ≅ SG*_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)·SL(2,Ẑ))/Σ.
- He states that (49) extends (45), which was first defined on the distinguished (normal) subgroup M_{0,3}^{!~} of index 6. Index 6 = |S_3| = |PSL(2,Z/2)|.

Purpose. The page lifts the GT-type action on the genus-0, 3-point group to the full S_3-symmetric group. Through the modular-group extension, this yields an action on profinite SL(2,Z) twisted by the elliptic tori. It is a step toward Section X on the next page, 'étude des groupes M_{ρ,σ} et de M_{ρ,σ} → Gl(2)'.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The page only states the decomposition and the extension without proof.

Compatibility (that (49) restricted to M^{!~} equals (45)) requires comparing the normalizations at 0 and at ω. These differ by an element of π̂_{0,3} (a path between base points), and the comparison is not written out. It is only defined modulo Σ, which is presumably why one passes to the quotient by Σ.

ideas.what: Semi-direct decomposition of the full automorphism group of π̂_{0,3} (with permutations of the punctures) as normalized automorphisms at a symmetric base point ⋊ the S_3-extension group
ideas.modern_name: Out*(F̂_2) ≅ (inertia-preserving part) ⋊ S_3; GT × S_3 type decompositions; normalization via a symmetric (tangential) base point
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the action on the Teichmüller tower and SL(2,Z) only in outline

ideas.what: Homomorphism from the (full) GT-type group M_{0,3}^~ to a semi-direct product of elliptic tori with profinite SL(2,Z), modulo signs, extending the map from the index-6 pure part
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT on the profinite modular group / on π̂_1^{orb}(M_{1,1}); GT ↔ PSL(2,Z) via M_{0,4}/S_3 = j-line
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura; Ihara–Matsumoto; Hain–Matsumoto for elliptic variants

missed.claim: This is an explicit (if unproved) construction of a GT-type action on profinite SL(2,Z), twisted by 'tori' attached to the elliptic points of orders 2 and 3 and taken modulo {±1}^3. It is extended from the pure index-6 part to the full S_3-symmetric automorphism group. The torus-twisted target M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) as an organizing object may be a formulation not explicitly in the literature, though the underlying action is known.
missed.quote: (49) M_{0,3}^~ → (M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) ≃ SG*_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ).Sl(2,Ẑ))_{/Σ} qui prolonge l'hom (45), défini d'abord sur ce sous-groupe distingué M_{0,3}^{!~} d'indice 6
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mild interest for the history of the GT/M_{1,1} connection. Grothendieck's explicit bookkeeping of the elliptic-point tori and of sign ambiguities might clarify the passage from GT to the automorphisms of SL(2,Ẑ), but it is mostly subsumed by Lochak–Schneps and Nakamura.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a short transitional page asserting a routine semi-direct splitting and an extension of an already defined homomorphism. The GT ↔ profinite SL(2,Z) link is well established in later literature; only the specific torus/sign formalism is unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: First line likely 'Mais on a aussi un produit semi-direct' (not 'Mais ... si').
In (48) the second factor is the hatted group Ĝ_{0,3}^+ (same symbol as on the previous page), not 𝔖_{0,3}^+.
'qui, continu directement à' likely reads 'qui, combiné directement à'.
In (49), 'M_{g,0}(Ẑ)' should be M_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ) and 'Sg_{g,σ}^*' should be SG*_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ).
'Sl(2,Ẑ)' corresponds to SL(2,Ẑ)' (with a prime) in the arrow from Ĝ_{0,3}^+.
